title: Dataset version registry
description: One dataset version: what every case's content hashed to, and who approved it. PRD §14.3: 'Formal dataset corrections create a new version and reason; they are not edited invisibly.' PRD §43.4: agents may not 'fix' a failing gold case by changing expected output without a versioned founder-approved reason. VERSIONED_CORRECTIONS compares the composed dataset against this registry, so an edit with no new version is a FAIL rather than a silent rewrite of history.
$comment: CONTENT HASH IS OVER CANONICAL JSON, NOT FILE BYTES. `core.autocrlf` is true on the maintainer's platform, so a file's bytes differ between Windows and Linux checkouts while its data does not; hashing the parsed document's canonical JSON form (sorted keys, no whitespace, UTF-8) is what makes a version registry reproducible across platforms. The sealed-envelope digest is over the decoded ciphertext bytes, which no checkout ever rewrites. VOCABULARY: inside the subset contracts.jsonschema_min implements.

version.description: The dataset version id, matching case.dataset_version.

approved_by.description: PRD §43.4's founder approval. A version with no approver is not a correction, it is an invisible edit.

reason.description: Why this version exists. PRD §14.3 requires the reason, not merely the version.

content_hash_salt.description: The per-version key for a BLIND case's `blind_content_sha256`. A blind case's content identity cannot be its ciphertext digest (a re-seal of identical plaintext changes it) and must not be a plain hash of the plaintext (that is a guess-confirmation oracle over blind content), so `seal` writes a KEYED blake2b digest under this salt and `VERSIONED_CORRECTIONS` compares those. Carried forward unchanged by `version new` — two versions with different salts have incomparable blind digests, which the check reports as UNRESOLVED rather than as a correction. Committed, not secret: it is a change detector, not a credential.
content_hash_salt.$comment: Rotating this value makes every blind digest incomparable with the previous version's on purpose; that is a Founder decision recorded in the version's `reason`.

supersedes.description: The version this one replaces, absent for the first version.

cases.description: One row per case in this version. Empty for the initial v1 registry, which exists so the ten authoring tickets add entries through the CLI rather than by hand-editing.

content_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the case's canonical JSON form — for a BLIND case, of its sidecar.

expected_output_sha256.description: SHA-256 over the expected-output members only (expected_answer_status, acceptable_statuses, gold_authorities, required/optional/prohibited_claims, expected_clarifications, expected_refusal_reason). A change here additionally requires a migration record (PRD §43.4), which is why it is hashed separately.

envelope_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the sealed ciphertext, for a BLIND case. Absent for a visible case. INFORMATIONAL ONLY: it changes on every re-seal of identical plaintext, so it is never used as a content identity — see `blind_content_sha256`.

blind_content_sha256.description: The keyed blake2b digest of the sealed PLAINTEXT under this registry's `content_hash_salt`, written by `seal` (the only step that holds blind plaintext). This is a BLIND case's content identity: it survives a re-seal, and it moves when the sealed case is corrected, which is what makes PRD §14.3's 'not edited invisibly' checkable for blind cases at all. A row without it is reported UNRESOLVED by VERSIONED_CORRECTIONS, never passed over.
